clue.text: Bird box has string

parts.note: to box is to spar, as boxers do in training
a string of things in a line is a row

explanation.surface: A birdhouse comes with a piece of string attached.
explanation.definitionFit: The house sparrow is a small, common brown songbird, so it is an example of a bird.

clue.text: Tasty dish mostly ordered with a starter of pasta

indicators.note: ordered means put into order, so the letters are arranged afresh
mostly means most of the word, so its final letter is dropped
the starter of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A tasty dish is mostly ordered along with a pasta starter.
explanation.definitionFit: Sapid is a rare word for having a pleasant, strong flavour, the opposite of insipid.

clue.text: One blackbird's heading over spot to sit on fence

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the earlier letters sit above the next piece

parts.note: A means one

indicators.note: a word's heading is its first letter

parts.note: a spot or mark is a stain

explanation.surface: A blackbird flies over a spot and perches on a fence.
explanation.walkthrough: To sit on the fence is to avoid taking sides.
explanation.definitionFit: To abstain is to decline to vote either way, which is what fence-sitters do.

clue.text: Smoke half of joint, then kip

indicators.note: half of means only the first three of six letters are used

parts.note: a reefer is a cannabis joint
the kip is the currency of Laos, abbreviated K

explanation.surface: Someone smokes half a joint and then has a nap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kip' is British slang for sleep, but here it is the Laotian currency.
explanation.definitionFit: Reek is Scots and northern English for smoke, as in Auld Reekie, a nickname for Edinburgh.

clue.text: Strange how he let Mrs sit back on chair for painting

indicators.note: strange means odd or unusual, so the letters are given an odd new order
the back of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: How odd that he let Mrs sit back in a chair to be painted.
explanation.walkthrough: The painting shows the artist's mother seated in a chair, so the surface describes it.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the popular title of James McNeill Whistler's portrait of his seated mother, a famous artwork.

clue.text: Order her gift and ring worker

indicators.note: to order things is to arrange them, so the letters of the words her gift are put into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone orders a present for a woman and phones a tradesman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ring' looks like a phone call but is the boxing ring, where this worker earns a living.
explanation.definitionFit: A boxer works in the ring, and a prizefighter is the usual name for one, so this is a playful description.

clue.text: Bond that's top secret

definitions.meaning: a stamp on classified papers meaning only the named reader may see them

explanation.definitionFit: It is the title of a 1981 James Bond film and also the classic marking on confidential documents.

clue.text: Setting out third piece in auction with a lot in the sale?

parts.note: going means departing or setting out

indicators.note: the third piece of a word is its third letter

parts.note: a heap of something is a lot of it

explanation.surface: Setting out a third lot at the auction sale.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods going cheap are being sold at a low price, as items in a sale are.

clue.text: Closed with maiden, cricketer we hear gets draw

parts.note: a door pushed to is closed
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

indicators.note: we hear means the word is spoken, its sound giving the letters

parts.note: a bowler is a cricketer who delivers the ball

explanation.surface: A cricket match is closed with a maiden and ends drawn.
explanation.walkthrough: Said with a British accent, bowler ends like BOLA. A tombola is a raffle from a drum, common at British fêtes.
explanation.definitionFit: A tombola is a lottery in which tickets are pulled from a revolving drum, so it is a kind of prize draw.

clue.text: Lives on borders

parts.note: re means on or concerning
the sides of something are its borders

explanation.surface: Someone lives on the edges.
explanation.definitionFit: To reside somewhere is to have your home there, a formal synonym.

clue.text: Office anger around men at the back

parts.note: a post is an office or position someone holds

indicators.note: around signals that the word for anger is turned round, read backwards

parts.note: ire is a literary word for anger
OR stands for 'other ranks', the ordinary soldiers, so men

explanation.surface: Office anger flares up over the staff working in the rear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' looks like a container signal for the men, but it only turns the anger backwards; OR then follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Posterior is an adjective for something situated behind or at the rear, a formal synonym.

clue.text: Bits of poetry from writer's American rubbish

parts.note: the writer of the clue says of themself 'I am', so writer's is I + AM
BS, short for bullshit, is American slang for rubbish or nonsense

explanation.surface: Some verses come from an author's trashy American work.
explanation.walkthrough: The writer is the setter, so 'writer's' expands to 'I am'.
explanation.definitionFit: An iamb is a metrical foot of one short and one long syllable, so these are small units of verse.

clue.text: Director hurt when going over shot

indicators.note: going over means turning over, so the word for hurt is read backwards

parts.note: to mar is to spoil or hurt

explanation.surface: A film director gets injured while doing a shot, perhaps a stunt.
explanation.definitionFit: A dram is a small drink of whisky, the same kind of measure as a shot.

clue.text: Keep stiff and carry on

parts.note: a stiff drink or stiff breeze is a strong one
to hold is to carry on or continue, as when good weather holds

explanation.surface: An instruction to stay firm and keep going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keep' reads as a verb but is the noun, the inner tower of a castle.
explanation.definitionFit: A castle's keep is its fortified central tower, so it is a fortress.

clue.text: Inside after going to pubs

parts.note: to come behind is to come after
bars are pubs

explanation.surface: Once inside, you go off to the pubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inside' is slang for in prison.
explanation.definitionFit: Being inside in slang means serving time in jail, the same as being locked up.

clue.text: Pick up one old lover for bit on the side?

indicators.note: to pick up a sound is to hear it, so the words are heard rather than read

parts.note: one gives AN and an old lover is an EX, so the phrase 'an ex'

explanation.surface: Someone resumes an affair with a former partner, a bit on the side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bit on the side' suggests an affair; it is really an extension built onto the side of a building.
explanation.definitionFit: An annexe is an extra building attached to a main one, quite literally a piece added at the side.

clue.text: Warms up again — run races to conserve energy

indicators.note: to conserve is to keep inside, so energy is held within the other letters

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for a run
heats are qualifying races
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: An athlete runs the qualifying rounds while saving energy for the final.
explanation.walkthrough: The E for energy sits between R and HEATS.
explanation.definitionFit: To reheat leftovers is to make them hot a second time, a direct synonym.

clue.text: See 21
Penny, excited with love, grabbing partner's bottom, having endless sex drive

indicators.note: grabbing means holding inside, so the next letter is taken in

parts.note: worked up means excited

indicators.note: a word's bottom is its last letter, as in a down clue

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which is O

indicators.note: endless means the final letter is cut off

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An excited Penny in love grabs her partner's backside, her sex drive unending.
explanation.walkthrough: Penny looks like a woman's name but gives P.
explanation.definitionFit: Drive means determination or a sense of aim, the same as purpose.

clue.text: He wrote notes by page with cryptic clue on

indicators.note: cryptic means obscure or puzzling, so the letters of clue and on are scrambled

explanation.surface: A setter writes notes beside a page with a cryptic clue on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'notes' are musical notes: the writer is a composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Francis Poulenc was a French composer, so a man whose writing was musical notes.

clue.text: Peer into 27 annual

indicators.note: into means the peer goes inside the two letters

parts.note: the answer to 27 across is a plural of the NATO phonetic code word for Y, so two Ys
an earl is a peer of the realm

explanation.surface: A nobleman looks into the annual report of the American baseball team.
explanation.walkthrough: In the NATO phonetic alphabet Yankee stands for Y, so the plural gives two Ys round EARL.
explanation.definitionFit: Something annual happens once a year, which is the adjective's meaning.

clue.text: Greenery in meadow following season

parts.note: a lea is a meadow
to season wood is to age it

explanation.surface: Greenery in a meadow after the season changes.
explanation.definitionFit: Leafage is foliage, the leaves of plants collectively.

clue.text: In ring take in swinging punch

parts.note: a ring is a round shape
to house someone is to take them in and give them shelter

explanation.surface: A boxer in the ring takes a wild swing.
explanation.definitionFit: A roundhouse is a wide, looping punch thrown with a big swing of the arm.

clue.text: Banks employed her pimp: any pros let go

indicators.note: let go means set loose, so the letters of pimp any pros run free into a new order

explanation.surface: Bankers hired a pimp, but the prostitutes were sacked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Banks' is not finance: it is the family of Mr and Mrs Banks in P. L. Travers's books.
explanation.definitionFit: In the stories the magical nanny is employed by the Banks family of Cherry Tree Lane to look after their children.

clue.text: More than one sure pharmacy's closing: couple of tablets needed?

indicators.note: a word's closing is its final letter
a couple of means two of them, so the tablets appear twice

parts.note: Es are ecstasy tablets

explanation.surface: Is the pharmacy shutting? A couple of pills might be needed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sure' as an exclamation means yes, so more than one is the plural.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying 'sure' is agreeing, so several such replies are agreements given out loud more than once.

clue.text: Local not for an alcoholic drink

definitions.note: a dialect word meaning against, opposed to

parts.note: gin is an alcoholic drink

explanation.surface: The local pub is not keen on alcoholic drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Local' says dialect: the word is regional English for against.
explanation.definitionFit: Agin is a dialect form of against, used locally for being opposed.

clue.text: Met in New York, perhaps old prince getting 'date'

parts.note: a date or period in history is an era

explanation.surface: An ageing prince meets his date in New York.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Met' looks like the past of meet; it is New York's Metropolitan Opera house.
explanation.definitionFit: The Met is the Metropolitan Opera of New York, an example of an opera company.

clue.text: What's limiting hairdressing? Girl's small mirror

parts.note: the letters at either end of the word hairdressing are H and G, read in full as 'H and G'
a lass is a girl, with the 's as 'is' joining it to the definition

explanation.surface: A girl's small mirror is all that holds back her hairdressing.
explanation.walkthrough: The limits of 'hairdressing' are H and G, and the word 'and' is written out in full.
explanation.definitionFit: A hand glass is a small mirror with a handle, held up to see the back of the head.

clue.text: One pardoning former addict smuggling cocaine

indicators.note: smuggling means carrying something hidden inside, so the cocaine letter goes within

parts.note: ex means former
a user is a drug addict
C is slang shorthand for cocaine

explanation.surface: A forgiving person turns out to be a reformed addict sneaking in drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: To excuse a fault is to pardon it, so someone who excuses is a pardoner.

clue.text: Americans pull and make out when going back

parts.note: to yank is to pull sharply

indicators.note: going back means the word for make out is read in reverse

parts.note: to make something out is to see it

explanation.surface: A couple pull each other close and kiss as they go home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pull' and 'make out' suggest romance; they are YANK and SEE.
explanation.definitionFit: Yankee is an informal name for anyone from the United States.
